ordered_diagnoses: Encephalitis due to Herpes Simplex Virus

s1.syndrome_frame: Altered mental status with focal neurological deficits and fever, progressing to obtundation
salient_findings: Left upper- and lower-limb weakness
Hypodense area in the right basal ganglia with mass effect on noncontrast head CT
T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in the right basal ganglia and internal capsule with mild surrounding edema on brain MRI
CSF with elevated WBCs, protein, and decreased glucose
Progression of neurological deficits and imaging findings despite empirical antibiotic treatment
key_facts: 19-year-old man with hepatitis C and intravenous heroin use
Altered mental status
Fever
Left upper- and lower-limb weakness (strength 2/5 and 3/5)
Glasgow Coma Scale 10
Required intubation for airway protection
Leukocytosis (white blood cell count rising from 10.0 to 14.6 × 10^3/µL)
Urine toxicology positive for benzodiazepines and opiates
Noncontrast head CT showed hypodense area in the right basal ganglia with mass effect
Brain MRI showed T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in the right basal ganglia and internal capsule
CSF with 538 WBCs/mm³ (57% polymorphonuclear leukocytes), protein 81 mg/dL, and glucose 57 mg/dL
Empirical IV ceftriaxone, vancomycin, and acyclovir were begun
Leukocytosis improved but fever persisted
Repeat lumbar puncture showed increased WBCs, protein, and decreased glucose
Repeat MRI demonstrated progression with new involvement of the left basal ganglia

shortlist: Encephalitis due to Herpes Simplex Virus

shortlist.label: Brain Abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Focal neurological deficits, fever, and hypodense area on head CT

shortlist.label: CNS Tuberculosis
shortlist.why_kept: Altered mental status, fever, and CSF findings consistent with infection

shortlist.label: Cerebral Toxoplasmosis
shortlist.why_kept: Focal neurological deficits, fever, and immunocompromised state due to hepatitis C

shortlist.label: Encephalitis due to Herpes Simplex Virus
shortlist.why_kept: Altered mental status, fever, and CSF findings consistent with viral infection

shortlist.label: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Immunocompromised state due to hepatitis C and intravenous heroin use, with progressive neurological decline

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, such as altered mental status, fever, and limb weakness, along with the imaging findings of hypodense areas in the basal ganglia and internal capsule, and the CSF analysis showing elevated WBCs, protein, and decreased glucose, are consistent with CNS tuberculosis, especially given the patient's history of intravenous heroin use which increases the risk of tuberculosis. The lack of response to empirical antibiotics and the progression of symptoms and imaging findings also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Brain Abscess
rejected.why: The absence of ring enhancement on MRI and the lack of significant improvement with empirical antibiotics make brain abscess less likely

rejected.label: Cerebral Toxoplasmosis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings are not typical for cerebral toxoplasmosis, which is more commonly seen in immunocompromised patients with HIV/AIDS

rejected.label: Encephalitis due to Herpes Simplex Virus
rejected.why: The negative PCR for herpes simplex virus and the lack of significant improvement with acyclovir make this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings are not consistent with PML, which typically presents with asymmetric white matter lesions and is seen in severely immunocompromised patients
